trancheRole: OLD-VITE React candidate. The migration story this corpus is built for is old-Vite to Vite 8, so an application whose ORIGIN bundler is Vite 2 is the required shape here, not a create-react-app or webpack candidate.

priorScout.role: read-only; supplied the target repository, tag, expected commit sha, and a set of claims about the tree
priorScout.reverificationPolicy: Every gate below was re-verified by this unit from the wire and from the reconciled archive at the pinned revision. The scout's findings were used as a hypothesis, not as evidence.

scoutClaimsCorrected.found: v0.1.3 is a LIGHTWEIGHT tag (ref object type `commit`), not an annotated one. The scout did not state a kind; this unit records the kind it observed.
scoutClaimsCorrected.materiality: low for identity (the commit sha is what is pinned), material for provenance language: there is no tagger, no tag message, and nothing to sign.

scoutClaimsCorrected.found: 120 files under web/src (149 blobs under web/ in total, 205 blobs in the whole repository).
scoutClaimsCorrected.materiality: none for the gate — the gate asks for a real substantive application, not a file count — but the scout's number is not reproduced and the observed number is what is recorded.

scoutClaimsCorrected.found: confirmed there is no .gitattributes at any depth, and additionally every one of the 205 extracted files was byte-scanned for a git-lfs pointer header. Zero found. LFS absence is established by scanning, not inferred.

scoutClaimsConfirmed: MIT LICENSE at repository root, blob 8b929a44e478b8969ee51e4d5ccb580b9372e939, 1062 bytes, 'Copyright (c) 2022 Memos'
React app under web/: vite ^2.9.0, @vitejs/plugin-react ^1.0.0, react ^18.1.0, typescript ^4.3.2, tailwindcss ^3.0.18, less ^4.1.1
no engines field, no packageManager field in web/package.json
web/yarn.lock is a yarn v1 lockfile of exactly 111922 bytes
a Go backend lives at the repository root and the frontend talks to it over same-origin /api/*

admitted.product: Memos — an open-source, self-hosted personal knowledge base / lightweight note ('memo') application backed by a SQLite file

evidence.manifestLicenseFieldNote: web/package.json declares no license field; yarn warned 'No license field' during install and run. The grant rests on the root LICENSE alone.
evidence.monorepoScoping: The licence is repository-root scoped and the ingest is web/-subtree scoped. There is no separate licence under web/. The ordinary reading — root MIT covers the whole repository including web/ — is recorded explicitly in license.json rather than left implicit.
evidence.quotedFromArchive: The licence text was read out of the extracted archive, which reconciles blob-for-blob with the git tree at the pinned revision.

evidence.repositoryShape: A Go/React monorepo: a Go HTTP server (echo) with a SQLite store at the repository root, and a Vite 2 React SPA under web/. The two are joined at runtime by same-origin /api/* calls; in development the Vite dev server proxies /api and /h/ to http://localhost:8080.
evidence.stateLayer: @reduxjs/toolkit 1.8 store with five slices (editor, location, memo, shortcut, user) plus a hand-written service layer under src/services (editorStateService, locationService, memoService, resourceService, shortcutService, userService)
domainSurface: memo compose / edit / pin / archive / delete
share-memo-as-image (a hand-rolled html2image lab under src/labs)
evidence.hasTestsNote: There is no test file anywhere under web/src and no test script in web/package.json. This is recorded as found; it is a real application without a front-end test suite, not a scaffold.
evidence.notes: The application is the product itself: a released v0.1.3 of a self-hosted product with a Docker image, a live demo, and a Go backend. It carries a hand-rolled markdown renderer (helpers/marked.ts), a filter DSL (helpers/filter.ts with TAG/TYPE/TEXT filter types and AND/OR relations), a usage heat map, and a dialog framework of its own (components/Dialog.tsx).

evidence.viteConfigShape: defineConfig with plugins: [react()] and a dev-server proxy for /api and /h/ to http://localhost:8080
evidence.entry: web/index.html with <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx">, the Vite 2 index-html-as-entry shape
evidence.noWebpack: no webpack, no react-scripts, no rollup config, and no babel config anywhere in the tree
evidence.originBundlerConfirmed: Vite 2.9.5, resolved from the repository's own committed lockfile rather than from a fresh resolution. This is a genuine old-Vite origin, which is the shape T006 requires.
evidence.buildProvenObservable: The Vite 2.9.5 bundler was run in this unit and produced a bundle — see baseline-attempt.json. Vite 2 is not merely declared here; it was exercised.

evidence.eraCoherence: Every era marker agrees on mid-2022: vite 2.9.5 (April 2022), react 18.1.0 (April 2022), typescript 4.6.3 (March 2022), tailwindcss 3.0.x, @reduxjs/toolkit 1.8, axios 0.27.2, esbuild 0.14.36. The lockfile's resolutions are all era-contemporary with the commit date, because the lockfile is committed and was not re-resolved.
evidence.upstreamStillActive: The upstream repository is not archived and has moved far past this revision. Only the pinned commit sha is immutable; the lightweight tag is a movable pointer upstream.
evidence.unknownPreserved: A lightweight tag has no tagger and no signature, so signer authenticity is recorded as unestablished, not resolved. The commit is also unsigned.

evidence.routerLibrary: none — the application ships a hand-rolled router (src/routers/index.ts, ~20 lines) with exactly two entries: "/signin" and "*" (Home). react-router is not a dependency.
evidence.journeyShapeCaveat: Because there are only two routes, this application's journeys are NOT route-driven. They are dialog- and state-driven inside a single Home page. Any later witness work must drive them through UI state, not through URL navigation. This is recorded as the material fact about this fixture's journey surface.

candidateJourneys.journey: search text and filter by tag
candidateJourneys.surface: SearchBar + TagList in the sidebar, MemoFilter above the list
candidateJourneys.code: src/components/SearchBar.tsx, src/components/TagList.tsx, src/components/MemoFilter.tsx, src/helpers/filter.ts (TAG/TYPE/TEXT filter types, CONTAIN / NOT_CONTAIN operators, AND/OR relations)
candidateJourneys.api: GET /api/tag; filtering itself is client-side over the loaded memo list

candidateJourneys.journey: archive a memo and restore it from the trash
candidateJourneys.surface: Memo card menu -> archive; MemoTrashDialog -> restore

candidateJourneys.journey: open settings and change account / preferences / members
candidateJourneys.surface: SettingDialog with three sections: my-account, preferences, and (admin only) member
candidateJourneys.note: The 'settings toggle' named in the packet is, at this revision, an export/import pair of buttons plus account and member administration; there is no theme or feature toggle in PreferencesSection. Recorded as found.

candidateJourneys.journey: create and apply a saved shortcut (a named filter query)
sign in / sign up and sign out
candidateJourneys.surface: the /signin page, the only real route

evidence.backendDependencyForJourneys: Every journey above requires the Go backend. Home.tsx calls userService.doSignIn() on mount and redirects to /signin unless a session is established, and axios is configured with withCredentials = true against same-origin /api. Nothing renders past the loading state without a backend.
evidence.unknownPreserved: These journeys are read from the components, the service layer, and the API helper. No browser was driven in this unit, so none of them is established as actually exercisable.

evidence.method: Every extracted regular file was checked for the `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/` pointer header, independently of whether any .gitattributes declares an LFS filter.
evidence.why: The factoriolab lesson: a tree can carry LFS pointers whose declaration is not visible in the ingest's own scope. Absence is scanned for, not assumed.

recordedRisks.risk: the declared build command fails at its typecheck gate, using only the repository's own pinned closure
recordedRisks.finding: `yarn build` expands to `tsc && vite build`. The `tsc` half exits 2 with four errors, all inside node_modules and none under src: TS2300 duplicate identifier 'LibraryManagedAttributes' and two TS2717 subsequent-property-declaration errors, arising because web/yarn.lock pins TWO copies of @types/react — 18.0.9 at the top level (from the direct ^18.0.9 range) and 18.0.5 nested under @types/react-dom (from its `@types/react "*"` dependency) — while web/tsconfig.json sets "skipLibCheck": false.
recordedRisks.consequence: This is NOT registry drift. yarn accepted --frozen-lockfile, so the failing tree is exactly the one the repository's committed lockfile declares. The declared build command did not succeed at this revision in this cell.

recordedRisks.risk: the bundler half of the build is unaffected by the typecheck failure
recordedRisks.finding: In one honestly-labeled deviation, esbuild's suppressed postinstall was run to bootstrap its platform binary and `vite build` was then run alone. It exited 0, transformed 898 modules, and emitted dist/index.html, a 263.69 KiB JS chunk, a 100.70 KiB CSS chunk, and 17 static icon/logo assets.
recordedRisks.consequence: The Vite 2 bundler works on this source. The failure is confined to the tsc gate. That is a favourable property for an old-Vite-to-Vite-8 migration fixture and it is recorded as an observation, not as a build success for the declared command.

recordedRisks.risk: the frontend cannot run without the Go backend
recordedRisks.finding: The web/ application has no client-side persistence and no mock layer. axios.defaults.withCredentials = true and every data call is same-origin /api/*. Home.tsx redirects to /signin unless userService.doSignIn() establishes a session. The dev server proxies /api and /h/ to http://localhost:8080.
recordedRisks.consequence: The web/ cell builds and bundles standalone, but no user journey is exercisable without a running Go backend and a SQLite store. Any later witness or browser unit must either stand up the Go backend (Go toolchain, out of this ingest's scope) or stub the /api surface.
recordedRisks.state: recorded; this is the dominant obstacle to browser-level work on this fixture

recordedRisks.risk: esbuild's platform binary depends on a lifecycle script
recordedRisks.finding: The baseline install ran with --ignore-scripts, which suppressed esbuild 0.14.36's install.js. The binary is shipped in the era-correct optional dependency esbuild-darwin-arm64@0.14.36, which the lockfile pins, so the deviation's bootstrap was a local link rather than a download.
recordedRisks.consequence: Any later unit that installs this fixture with lifecycle scripts disabled must bootstrap esbuild before the bundler will run.

recordedRisks.finding: yarn warned 'No license field' on both install and run. The MIT grant is carried only by the repository-root LICENSE.
recordedRisks.consequence: Nothing inside web/ corroborates the licence. Any artifact derived from the web/ subtree must carry the root MIT notice explicitly.

recordedRisks.finding: There is no test file under web/src and no test script in web/package.json.
recordedRisks.consequence: There is no upstream behavioural oracle for this fixture. Any migration evidence must come from a Versionless-built oracle, not from the repository's own suite.

recordedRisks.risk: the repository's declared Node cell was not reproduced
recordedRisks.finding: The repository DOES declare a build cell, in the Dockerfile's frontend stage: `FROM node:14.18.2-alpine3.14`, then `RUN yarn` and `RUN yarn build`. The scout's 'no engines, no packageManager' is correct as far as package.json goes, but it is not the whole story — the Dockerfile is the declaration. This unit ran on Node 16.20.2 darwin-arm64 instead, because Node 14 has no darwin-arm64 build at all and honouring 14.18.2 here would require Rosetta 2 (which would also switch esbuild to its x64 binary) or a linux container.
recordedRisks.consequence: Every baseline outcome in this ingest is labelled era-consistent rather than repository-pinned. Whether the tsc failure also occurs under Node 14.18.2 alpine is not tested and not claimed.

recordedRisks.risk: the upstream tag is lightweight and the repository is still active
recordedRisks.finding: refs/tags/v0.1.3 points directly at the commit with no tag object. The repository is not archived and its main line has moved far past this revision.
recordedRisks.consequence: The tag is a movable pointer upstream; only the commit sha 565fe0cc567c02deb59fc04830df707ea7476d52 and the archive digest recorded here are immutable.

nonclaims: Admission fixes an identity and records gate findings. It establishes no browser behavior, journey exercisability, migration feasibility, pilot status, production readiness, certification, or legal approval.
The journey list is read from the components and the service layer; no journey was driven in a browser by this unit.
The Go backend was neither built nor run. Its presence and its /api surface are recorded from the source only.
No adapter, transform, or migration lane is declared for this fixture by the unit that ingested it.
